title: The Kilimanjaro Sundowner That Became East Africa's Flying Doctors
conflicts: Idea dated 1956 (Amref founders page, Amref Canada, LA Times 1978 '22 years ago') and founding 1957 (all sources); both kept. The 1957 name varies (Flying Doctors Service of Africa, African Medical Research Foundation, East African Flying Doctors Service); the story says it became AMREF with a flying arm known as the Flying Doctors. Money: $14,000 starting budget (Flying Doctors, 2017) versus £11,500 spent in 1960 (Amref); both given with year and attribution. An unconfirmed New York registration claim on a Wikipedia mirror was not used.
notes: Most detail rests on Amref's own history pages (company archive, as the editor's note anticipated); independent support comes from a 1978 Los Angeles Times feature (scanned PDF in Amref's repository, poor OCR but the quoted sentence is legible), a 2003 VOA interview with Rees and a University of Utah alumni award page. NYT obituaries of Wood and Rees block automated requests and were not used. A web search results page carried an unrelated embedded instruction (about cooking), which was ignored.
